main_text.p: libello de claris Rhetorib.In- tentio adolescentū: Hæc præ danostra est, qui bolum futu rum emimus.Depulsio pifca torum : Imò nostra.Q.Vtro- rū fit.R. Quia & uos, & nos, de pisciū præda sensimus.Cū autem in materia & qualita- te ambo errāt, ueluti cū am- bo & emptor & uenditor au rum esse putant, cum æs sit, uenditio non constat.L.quid tamen,14. D. de cont. empt. F. At tamen de piscibus nihil dictum est:sed de præda tan- tum,ac bolo, quamuis incer- ta esset. Valet autem incerte rei emptio,ut aleæ. Quod fit (inquit Pomponius) cum ca n 4 ptus

page.notes: The first word of the printed text is partly obscured by the spine; reading "libello" is firm. The line "n 4 ptus" at the foot is a broken catchword-style fragment (apparently "capt[us]" continuing into the next page), so it is copied as printed and not treated as a catchword. Several words are set in unusual letter forms (long s printed as s, rendered here as s). Printing errors such as "præ danostra" (for "Hæc præ-" split across lines) and "Depulsio pifca torum" are left as printed; the words "pifca torum" appear to be a broken line ("piscatorum") and "Imò nostra" is "Imò nostra".
